references.text: Describes the same atonement ritual for the sanctuary, the tent of meeting, and the altar mentioned in verse 33
Refers to atonement (כפר) made for the people, the same concept as in 16:33
Aaron shall make atonement on the horns of the altar once a year, pointing toward the annual Day of Atonement described in Leviticus 16
Atonement for the altar and its consecration, parallel to the atonement of the altar in 16:33
Prophetic vision concerning atonement for the temple, reflecting the atonement ritual for the sanctuary
Atonement for the priests, the same group mentioned in 16:33
The high priest enters the Most Holy Place once a year with blood for himself and the sins of the people, fulfilling the Day of Atonement ritual
Explains that the earthly sanctuaries had to be cleansed with blood, while the heavenly ones with a better sacrifice - pointing back to the atonement ritual in Leviticus 16
Describes the Day of Atonement (Yom Kippur) when atonement is to be made, the same festival that 16:33 is part of
The sacrifices on the Day of Atonement made for atonement for the people
